about: Hand-authored reference behaviors and known defects of the two HTML demos (INV-0003). Every entry cites anchors: {demo, line, contains} means the given line of the demo contains the snippet; {demo, absent} means the snippet occurs nowhere in that demo. tests/contracts/test_reference_fixtures.py verifies every anchor against the pinned demo files. Literal constants live in demo_constants.json (extracted, not hand-copied).

tp.note: Pinned S2 behavioral reference, archived 2026-10-06; the live playable-mock template is now demos/template/investigators_demo.html.

behaviors.summary: Active task budget: TP reference 360 s counted by a 1 s browser interval that decrements only while not paused. The revised PE reference (2026-10-01) uses 480 s (8 minutes) and has no pause guard. The production task stays at 360 s (UX feedback item 13 — the demo's 8-minute value is deliberately not adopted).

System chat message "One minute left." at 60 s remaining (active second 300); timer switches to its low-time style for the final 60 s. Only in-task time warning. Server equivalent: warning.one_minute_left v1 on the active_task clock.
Task ends only at timeout; there is no early final submission. Answers are recorded on every picker change.

Eight crates, six hideouts; four assigned crates shown in ascending order; roles shuffled as own, own, team, team. The revised PE reference (2026-10-01) keeps the same generator semantics but is a const/let rewrite, so the two demos are no longer byte-identical.
Each crate walks three distinct hideouts (legA -> legB -> truth). Own-file crates make their final move yesterday 11:00-14:00; team-dependent and unassigned crates make it today 11:30-14:00.

anchors.contains: var walk = shuffled(HIDEOUTS).slice(0, 3); // legA -> legB -> truth

behaviors.summary: Participant information cutoffs: one own crate ends yesterday 20:00 and the other today 15:00; one team crate ends yesterday 20:00 and the other today 09:30. Assigned-crate entries after the cutoff go to JT or PM by an independent fair coin per entry.
For each unassigned crate the participant holds the last two entries at or after today 12:00 (useful to teammates, useless to the participant); every other entry goes to JT or PM by a fair coin.

Initial case-file order is a uniform shuffle; entries can be reordered by drag; shared entries go to both teammates; the assistant reads only entries currently in the participant's file; team entries enter the file only via Add to case file; entries cannot be dragged to the assistant.
A share counts as proactive when it concerns a crate that is not the participant's, has not been requested by a teammate, and was not made from a request's Share intel prompt.

Scripted teammate requests: two for distinct unassigned crates (first and third) and one for an assigned crate (second); seats are a shuffle of JT, PM, JT so JT asks twice and PM once in every session. Timing: TP reference 40/150/240 active seconds; the revised PE reference (2026-10-01) uses 60/180/300.
A participant request returns exactly one record: the latest entry for that crate across JT's and PM's holdings, sent by whichever seat holds it; nothing is sent if neither holds an entry.

anchors.contains: var order = jt && pm ? parseStamp(jt.stamp) >= parseStamp(pm.stamp) ? [jt, pm] : [pm, jt]

behaviors.summary: Delay distribution delay(lo,hi): lognormal around the midpoint (lo+hi)/2 with sigma 0.45 (Box-Muller), clamped to [lo, 2.2*hi] seconds.
Structured record reply (teammate share in answer to a request): wall-clock setTimeout of delay(5,12) + min(9000 ms, 28 ms per visible character). Not paused by the TP check-in.

anchors.contains: var wait = delay(lo, hi) + Math.min(9000, chars * 28);

behaviors.summary: Greeting: prompt appears 2 s after start (tracked timeout); JT replies after delay(1.5,3)+typing, PM after delay(3.5,5) then delay(1,2)+typing (wall clock).

Free-text teammate reply (the only generative teammate turn): model call with 25 s abort, THEN an additional wall-clock delay(4,10) + min(8000 ms, 35 ms per character) after the response arrives, so model latency is additive.
Assistant reply: 20 s timeout; a display floor of delay(2,4) measured from the moment of asking (not additive to model latency); offline analyzer path waits delay(3,7).

Time-pressure check-in at active second 60: active clock pauses; participant rates own pressure 1-7; 3.5 s simulated collection (wall clock); teammate values revealed (high 6/7, low 2/3; higher value to JT or PM by fair coin); explicit Resume; values stay visible above the chat.

anchors.contains: How much time pressure do you feel while working on this task right now?
Your rating will be visible to your teammates.
These ratings will stay visible above the team chat.

behaviors.summary: Requests and prompts are possible before the check-in (the 40 s request precedes it); counts before/after the check-in are logged.

Peer-evaluation exposure surfaces (eval arm): intro callout, instructions reminder, persistent task-header strip, system message at task start, peer-rating intro. Control arm: generic questionnaire wording, no strip, no system message.

Seat voices: the revised PE reference (2026-10-01) removed the scripted thanks/noNews/afterShare pools — thread replies are generative when TEAMMATE_LIVE is set, otherwise a canned teammateFallback pool drawn with rand() (repeats allowed).

The probabilistic share-acknowledgment layer (ACK_P seat asymmetry, prompted/unprompted ack probabilities, delay(4,12) acks) was removed in the revised PE reference (2026-10-01): shares receive no teammate reply in the demo.
The +28-active-second crosstalk follow-up layer was removed in the revised PE reference (2026-10-01).
Peer ratings of JT and PM (1-7 helpfulness) are collected after confidence in BOTH arms; the demo requires both ratings before Continue.
The peer-evaluation demo has no time-pressure check-in.
Confidence 0-100 per answered crate only; the slider starts at 50 but a crate counts as rated only after the participant moves it; unanswered crates show 'No location selected.'

Code comment says one unowned crate is never requested; with four unassigned crates and two distinct unassigned requests, TWO remain unrequested. Use generated allocations to define opportunities (spec §2.1).
Browser Math.random generates the world, record order, seat choices and delays; the full world including truth lives in participant JavaScript (spec §2.3).

Unknown or missing condition silently defaults to high pressure (TP) or evaluation (PE); spec §4 requires rejecting unknown combinations. The condition chooser and Restart are exposed in the demo banner.

Teammate messages, free-text replies, acknowledgments and the check-in reveal use setTimeout callbacks that are not in the tracked timeouts list: they are not cleared by endTask and keep running during the check-in pause, so they can land after closure or during the pause (spec §2.3).
AI reply logging records fallback:false before the validation decision that may return the analyzer fallback (spec §2.3).
Browser calls an external relay (qualtrics-relay.example.com/chatgpt) and pre-warms it; model output is validated only by hideout-name matching (spec §2.3).
Completion relies on INV_FINISH writing embedded data and a 1.2 s flush delay before auto-advancing (spec §2.3).
Post-task demo items style the chosen button but never save the response (spec §2.3).

Historical: crosstalk treated a share_prompted event (the participant merely opened the Share intel prompt) as answered, so an afterShare line could follow a request that received no share. The 2026-10-01 PE rewrite removed the crosstalk layer entirely, so the defect mechanism no longer exists in the demo.
If the participant's initials equal a seat label, that teammate is silently renamed AR in display only.
Peer ratings are forced (Continue disabled until both are given), conflicting with the approved protocol's permission to skip questions (spec §13 'Optional answers'; D06).

Both demos advertise a $0.25-per-correct-crate bonus (max $1.00) that the approved protocol does not select (D04); the PE debrief says no one rated the participant, which must be reconciled with the eval-arm expectation (D03).
